name: State Street
description: State Street is a custody bank: it holds and administers $53.8 trillion of assets for institutional investors and charges servicing fees on them (5.3 billion in 2025), plus fees for foreign exchange trading, securities lending and software, and net interest on $274 billion of deposits. Investment Servicing is 81 percent of revenue; Investment Management (State Street Investment Management, including SPDR ETFs) runs $5.67 trillion of AUM and earns management fees, 19 percent of revenue. Fee revenue was $11.0 billion and net interest income $3.0 billion of $13.9 billion total, so it behaves like an asset-based fee business with a bank balance sheet.

businessLines.name: Investment Servicing
businessLines.how: Institutional clients (asset managers, pension funds, insurers) pay servicing fees, a few basis points on assets under custody (5,324), plus fees for FX trades (1,441), securities lending (481), software and processing (927), and the bank earns net interest on the deposits (2,945).

businessLines.name: Investment Management
businessLines.how: Management fees (2,398) charged as a percentage of assets in ETFs (including the SPDR range), index funds and institutional mandates; FX trading and other fees are small add-ons.

geography.method: Regional revenue tagged in the filing's own XBRL instance: full-year contexts with one geographic dimension (or segments named after places), alone or crossed only with operating segments or a revenue line of the income statement; regions must add up to the revenue line within 1 percent; a member equal to the sum of others is a subtotal; the main split is the largest set of members adding up to the total; anything not broken out is a computed remainder.
